title: The Little Trucks Who Move the Moon | Calm Bedtime Story
description: Have you ever wondered how the Moon climbs into the sky each night? It's the little trucks! Every evening, a tiny crew of friendly trucks gently moves the big round Moon up over the hills and sets it softly among the stars, so it can shine on all the sleeping children. A slow, magical bedtime story for little ones who love trucks and the Moon. New stories every week.
narration:
Have you ever wondered how the Moon gets up into the sky?

Well. I'll tell you a secret. It's the little trucks who move the Moon.

Every evening, when the sky turns soft and pink and the day grows sleepy, the big round Moon waits at the bottom of the hill. It is much too big to climb up by itself. So the little trucks come to help.

There is little Pip, the smallest truck, with the kindest eyes. There is round Bo, who hums a gentle tune. And there is tall, quiet Nell, slow and strong and gentle.

"It's time," whispered Pip. "Time to move the Moon."

Softly, ever so softly, the little trucks rolled up to the big round Moon. They leaned against it with their soft round bumpers. And gently — oh, so gently — they began to push.

rrm… rrm… rrm…

Up the hill they went, slow as slow can be. The Moon rolled forward just a little. Then a little more. The little trucks did not hurry. You can never hurry the Moon.

rrm… rrm… rrm…

Up, and up, and up the gentle hill, until at last they reached the very top, where the sky was wide and dark and waiting.

The little trucks stopped to catch their breath. The stars were already out, twinkling softly, holding a place for the Moon.

"Ready?" hummed Bo.

"Ready," said Nell.

And together, slow and careful, the little trucks lifted the big round Moon up… up… up… and set it ever so softly onto its cushion of stars.

There.

The Moon settled into the sky with a happy little glow. And all at once, its soft white light spilled down over the whole wide world — over the hills, over the trees, over the rivers and the rooftops, over every sleepy little child tucked up warm in bed.

The little trucks looked up at the Moon they had moved, glowing high and round and beautiful, and they felt very proud and very, very sleepy.

Their job was done.

Slowly, they rolled back down the gentle hill to their cosy little shed. Pip yawned. Bo's hum grew soft and slow. Nell's engine went rrm… rrm… shhhhh.

And one by one, the little trucks who move the Moon curled up together and closed their eyes, safe and snug, while the Moon they lifted kept watch over the sleeping world.

Goodnight, little Pip. Goodnight, round Bo. Goodnight, tall quiet Nell.

Goodnight, big round Moon, shining softly in the sky.

And goodnight to you. Sleep now. The Moon is up. Everything is calm. Everything is well.
